blocks.name: Market west: civic and trade
blocks.front: Existing square and west market approach
blocks.rear: Shared service court reached from the halt-side back lane
blocks.edge: Plot gardens behind the court, not grass between every frontage
blocks.role: Library, bakery and herbalist stay recognisable; two existing shop records close the approach and market corner.

blocks.name: Market east: trades and the green
blocks.front: Existing east side of the square and harbour-road approach
blocks.rear: Smithy working side and separate domestic/service plots
blocks.edge: Existing green/training space and crater remain open; riverbank fit unresolved
blocks.role: Keep the old smithy and Fern cottage identities; a shop and two house records make a short connected approach frontage.

blocks.name: Garden approach and north terrace
blocks.front: Existing garden walk and the north side of the market approach
blocks.rear: Quiet plot backs and garden access
blocks.edge: Cultivated garden edge toward the existing northern approach
blocks.role: Your hut and north terrace cottages remain anchors; two added records define the arrival without enclosing the quiet garden in a busy goods court.

blocks.name: West Lane: mixed fronts and deep plots
blocks.front: Short runs on West Lane connected to the market-west approach
blocks.rear: A continuous back/service lane with individual courts and long garden plots
blocks.role: The two row-house records provide grouped frontage; cottages and a house turn the corner and taper the grain toward the edge.

blocks.name: Eastgate: inns and coach court
blocks.front: Connected eastern arrival and inn fronts
blocks.rear: One legible coach/service court behind the principal inn; a smaller separate inn court
blocks.edge: Route approaches and cultivated edge, not an isolated paved slab
blocks.role: Retain both inn records. The larger-facing inn fronts the coach court; other existing house/cottage records connect Eastgate to the town.

blocks.name: Mill End: street, grain court and lower plots
blocks.front: Short connected groups along Mill Street and its lower junction
blocks.rear: Side passages to plot courts and a shared grain-handling approach
blocks.edge: Sleepwater bank and productive gardens/farms, with working court kept distinct
blocks.role: Existing house/cottage forms surround the existing mill/grain programme. One separately listed proposed mill representation restores the omitted programme; original ten records and smithy are unchanged. Candidate building identity and native fit remain unresolved.

blocks.name: Halt Road: inhabited productive fringe
blocks.front: Halt approach with visible connections back to the market
blocks.rear: Long gardens and small work plots served from the goods side
blocks.edge: Halt-related working space and farms beyond
blocks.role: A small connected housing group explains the approach. Rail loading remains a separate yard, never relabelled as an inn coach court.
